mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (RSAFS) indicates strong household confidence and spending, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE decline and PAYEMS rise) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO decline > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as corporate production and earnings face headwinds, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% qoq.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,350,000 units, it signals strong residential construction and household spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1350.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust demand for housing and related sectors, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS rise and HOUST rise) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive returns due to strong consumer spending, but this effect is amplified when payroll employment (PAYEMS) is rising rapidly (by more than 100,000 jobs).
regime_hint: low unemployment with strong job growth
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS rises by more than 100,000 jobs.
